name: nom-supreme
description: Error-handling and ergonomics extension layer on top of nom

license.comment: Cargo.toml declares license = "MPL-2.0"; single license on every published version.

approach.comment: Per Assessment Guidelines. Self-described 'collection of excellent utilities for nom': ParserExt postfix combinators, ErrorTree, enhanced tag, parse_separated_terminated, final_parser. Not a parser framework on its own; requires nom.

implementation.comment: Dependencies are nom, memchr, brownstone, indent_write and joinery, all pure-Rust crates; no C/C++ build step.

documentation.comment: README is a one-liner pointing at docs.rs; no book or site.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; 0.8.0 published 2022-04-21. All research reflects 0.8.0, which depends on nom >=6.0.1, <8.0.0 — it does not build against nom 8 (issue #18 open, PR #19 unmerged).

grammar-class.comment: Inherited from nom: combinators impose no formal grammar class (per Assessment Guidelines); nom-supreme adds no grammar restrictions.

grammar-definition.comment: Parsers are nom functions/closures; ParserExt adds postfix method syntax (.terminated(), .context(), .cut(), ...) but the grammar is still plain Rust.

left-recursion.comment: No precedence/Pratt helper in any module (context, error, final_parser, multi, parser_ext, tag); left recursion must be eliminated by hand as in plain nom. nom-language's precedence module targets nom 8, which nom-supreme 0.8 cannot be combined with.

ambiguity-handling.comment: Inherited from nom's alt; nom-supreme's ErrorTree::Alt additionally records every failed alternative when all branches fail.

backtracking.comment: Unlimited by default; ParserExt::cut (and parse_from_str_cut) converts recoverable errors into failures to commit to a branch.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless like nom: the enhanced tag parsers and ParserExt operate directly on any nom input type (InputLength/InputTake/Compare bounds).

precedence-pratt-support.comment: No operator-precedence facility among the crate's modules.

unicode-aware.comment: Inherited from nom's &str handling (char-level primitives, UTF-8 boundary-safe slicing). nom-supreme's own final_parser::Location (line/column) is implemented for &str only; PR #15 adding [u8] support is unmerged.

input-types.comment: Generic over nom's input traits, so &str, &[u8] and custom inputs work. Line/column Location is &str-only; ByteOffset works for any input implementing nom's Offset.

streaming-partial-input.comment: Inherited from nom's streaming combinators (Err::Incomplete). Note final_parser deliberately wraps the parser in .complete() so Incomplete becomes an error at the entry point.

zero-copy.comment: Inherited from nom; ParserExt::recognize / with_recognized return slices of the input via the Offset trait without copying.

span-tracking.comment: Errors carry the remaining input at the failure point (a single position, not a range). final_parser's RecreateContext/ExtractContext convert it to ByteOffset (any Offset input) or Location {line, column} (1-indexed, &str only). No wrapper input type needed, unlike nom_locate.

output-model.comment: Parsers return arbitrary user types; final_parser bridges IResult to a plain Result<O, E>.

semantic-actions.comment: ParserExt adds postfix map_res, value, parse_from_str, verify, array, separated_array on top of nom's map family.

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: No implicit skip rules; whitespace is consumed explicitly, e.g. .terminated(space0) / .delimited_by(...).

stateful-parsing.comment: Same borderline position as nom: no dedicated state parameter, but parsers are closures that can capture mutable state, and parse_separated_terminated threads a user accumulator through a fold. Not a first-class API.

error-recovery.comment: Improves error *reporting*, not recovery: parsing still stops at the first Err::Error/Err::Failure; no skip-to-sync or pluggable recovery API.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: One failure per run. ErrorTree::Alt aggregates the alternatives tried at a single failure point and Stack records the context chain, but these describe one error, not independent errors at multiple locations.

expected-token-reporting.comment: ErrorTree's BaseErrorKind::Expected(Expectation) records what was expected (Tag with the literal expected, Char, Digit, Alpha, Eof, ...); the TagError trait lets the enhanced tag parser report the exact expected tag, and Alt lists every alternative that was tried. This is the crate's headline improvement over nom's VerboseError.

custom-error-types.comment: Inherits nom's generic error parameter; nom-supreme's TagError and ContextError traits are implementable for user types, and GenericErrorTree is generic over tag, context and external-error types.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Each ErrorTree node carries a single location (the input tail), convertible to a ByteOffset or a line/column Location. No byte ranges and no labelled secondary spans, so 3 per the guideline.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets dependency or documented bridge; ErrorTree implements Display (indented tree rendering via indent_write/joinery) and std::error::Error.

contextual-error-messages.comment: ParserExt::context and the context module attach labels of any Clone type (not just &'static str) via the ContextError trait; ErrorTree::Stack keeps the full chain.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No tree reuse; same as nom.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Produces user-defined values; no CST facility.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: lib.rs reverse-dependency list (98 crates, checked 2026-09-19) contains no editor or language server.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: No independent benchmark of nom-supreme found (searched 2026-09-19); it is not included in epage/parse-benchmarks-rs. As a thin layer over nom its happy-path cost should track nom, but ErrorTree allocates Vec/Box on failure paths, so no tier is asserted.

compile-time-impact.comment: No build-time measurement or issue found (2026-09-19). Five small pure-Rust dependencies and no proc-macros suggest a light delta, but per the guideline a guess is not recorded.

allocation-strategy.comment: parse_separated_terminated is fold-based and allocation-free (collect_separated_terminated allocates via Extend); ParserExt combinators are zero-cost wrappers. ErrorTree itself allocates (Vec for Stack/Alt, Box<dyn Error> for external errors) on the failure path.

generated-code-size.comment: Combinator extension; no code generation. No source: follows from the approach.

no-std-support.comment: lib.rs has no no_std attribute (only #![deny(missing_docs)]); 0.8.0 removed all feature flags, the changelog says they 'may come back ... until someone cites a desire for nom-supreme in a no-std context', and issue #11 (Sep 2022) requesting no_std is open without a response.

msrv.comment: No rust-version in Cargo.toml (edition 2018) and no MSRV statement in the README or docs; crates.io lists rust_version as null for every version.

unsafe-usage.comment: No `unsafe` found in lib.rs, error.rs, final_parser.rs, tag.rs, parser_ext.rs, multi.rs or context.rs (the whole crate), but no `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` is declared, so tagged minimal rather than forbid, consistent with other candidates.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: Trait/function API plus one declarative macro (express!); no proc-macro or syn dependency.

dependency-count.comment: nom (>=6.0.1, <8.0.0), memchr, brownstone, indent_write, joinery. Dev-only: cool_asserts.

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: pure Rust, std-only, no platform-specific code or FFI, so wasm32-unknown-unknown (which has std) should work; not verified in the crate's CI.

async-friendly.comment: Parsers are plain closures over slices; ErrorTree's external error type is Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync + 'static>, so errors cross async boundaries. No async API of its own.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads as of 2026-09-19 (~397k/month per lib.rs); 98 dependent crates, 37 directly.

maintenance-status.comment: Last commit and release both 2022-04-21; the nom 8 upgrade request (issue #18, Feb 2025) and PR #19 (May 2025) plus the no_std request (#11, 2022) have no maintainer response. Repo is not archived and no successor is named. Retagged from passively-maintained to dormant on 2026-09-20 after the tag was added; treat as unmaintained for nom 8 users.

documentation-quality.comment: docs.rs API docs are complete (#![deny(missing_docs)]) with module-level explanations and examples for ParserExt, ErrorTree and final_parser; README is a single line (the maintainer's own issue #16 'Need a readme' is open) and there is no tutorial or migration guide.

notable-users.value: symbolic-debuginfo (Sentry, breakpad feature), cargo-contract transcode (use-ink), rs-matter-codegen (project-chip)
notable-users.comment: Verified from each project's Cargo.toml (symbolic-debuginfo: optional under the breakpad feature; cargo-contract pins 0.7.0 with the error feature; rs-matter-codegen 0.8).

bus-factor.comment: Nathan West (Lucretiel) is the sole crates.io owner and author of every commit in the recent history.
